claims.statement: Code is grouped by domain (DDD-influenced layout, TES-68) into four layers — app/ thin routes, modules/<domain>/{data,domain,ui} with one module per PRD FR (14 domains, matching the modules/ directory), shared/ as the leaf level, and lib/supabase/ as the external data boundary — and new code goes inside its owning module rather than in a new top-level folder.

No business logic lives in app/ (review-level rule): Server Components fetch through a module's data/ layer and compose module ui/ over shared/ui primitives, which is why the dashboard and billing routes import data/, domain/ and ui/ surfaces of several modules side by side.
The import direction app → modules → shared → lib/supabase is ESLint-enforced via import/no-restricted-paths zones in eslint.config.mjs covering the app/, modules/, shared/, and lib/ trees.

Another module's data/ is private to every other module: its public surface is domain/ + ui/, and only app/ may fetch from any module's data/; the lint zones are generated per domain from the 14-entry domains array in eslint.config.mjs.

shared/ is the leaf level and must never import modules/ or app/ (lint-enforced) nor lib/supabase/database.types (README rule): it holds the single-file shared/types.ts UI domain types, props-only shared/ui/ primitives (a shared/ui component that starts reading data or encoding business rules moves to its owning module), shared/vocab.ts (closed TESDA vocabulary that stays in shared/ because consumers live in two modules), and shared/text.ts (pure copy shaping). shared/mocks/ was deleted entirely in the mock-data retirement even though shared/README.md still lists it.

Only module data/ layers (besides lib/supabase itself) may import lib/supabase/database.types.ts; app/, shared/, and modules' ui/ and domain/ are lint-blocked from raw DB row types and must import domain types instead.

Two type families stay deliberately separate: lib/supabase/database.types.ts (raw rows — Row/Insert/Update for 18 tables, seven Postgres enums, three RPC signatures, Views empty) and hand-written shared/types.ts (UI domain types, with Batch as a hub referencing shapes from six other domains). The mappers in module data/ layers are the only seam between them; module-scoped non-cross-domain types (Profile) live in that module's domain/ and reuse shared types rather than inventing a second vocabulary.

Every entity contract follows fetch → map → derive per the reference implementation modules/batches/data/batches.ts: fetch is a typed Supabase query whose rows are scoped by RLS (never manually filtered by tenant in JS), map is a pure DB-row to domain translation, derive computes lifecycle/date helpers.

mapBatchRow is pure (no I/O), exported for unit tests, and marks schema gaps with TODO(contract) defaults so the UI shape stays valid — e.g. billingDeadline and daysToBilling stand in on end_date because no billing_deadline column exists yet.

Every read contract returns a four-state discriminated snapshot: ok (mapped rows + dataAsOf = freshest updated_at), no-tenant-access, sync-failed (Supabase configured but the query errored or the client construction threw — error string kept server-side), and unconfigured (isSupabaseConfigured() false). Since the mock-data retirement no state substitutes mock or fabricated data: selectBatchesForDisplay returns snapshot.batches only for ok and [] for every other state; unconfigured renders an honest empty state with no banner, sync-failed renders the same empty state plus the sync-failed banner. The throwing getBatches() wrapper converts every non-ok state into an exception.

Modules extend the four-state union only with genuinely distinct outcomes and vary the ok payload per contract: tenancy's ProfileSnapshot adds not-found (authenticated with Clerk but no profiles row yet — webhook raced or failed, 'no access yet' rather than an error), import-export's LearnerImportSnapshot adds validation-failed with errors[] decided before any Supabase client is created (partially valid files return ok with a skipped list), and ActivitySnapshot's ok arm carries hasMore derived by fetching one row beyond the requested limit instead of a count query.

Raw error strings never reach the UI: a real sync failure with zero rows renders the fixed-copy SyncFailedView ('Couldn't reach Supabase' / 'Batch data isn't available right now…') with only a ' from <data-as-of>' fragment appended, never snapshot.error. The inline SyncFailedCallout's 'showing the last cached snapshot' branch is a mock-era remnant — isShowingCachedFallback can only be true when the snapshot is not ok, which now always yields zero rows and takes the full-page screen, so a live-rows banner reads 'the currently loaded data'.

DB_TO_UI_STAGE in modules/batches/data/batches.ts is a total (non-Partial) enum-bridge map so a new DB enum variant fails compilation until its UI treatment is chosen: training/assessment/billing map to UI train/assess/bill, entre is UI-only with no DB column, completed/blocked map to null and are special-cased by deriveLifecycle (all stages done / no stage active), and normalizeStatus surfaces DB blocked as UI pending.

The total-map bridge convention repeats across data layers — STAGE_TO_UI (documents), ACTION_TO_TONE (activity), DB_TO_UI_ROLE (tenancy, DB profile_role a strict subset of UI UserRole), UI_TO_DB_ROLE (tenancy users.ts, the write-direction bridge), ASSESSMENT_RESULT_TO_UI (learners, pending to '') — while DOCUMENT_ICONS is deliberately a Partial map with a generic fallback because document_key is per-program configured data, not a closed enum.

Because a module's data/ is private, batches.ts hand-duplicates documents.ts's mapper logic (MISSING_DOC, mapDocumentRow, the catalog backfill in mapDocumentsMap/mapDocumentRows), kept in sync by hand rather than imported; activity.ts's toRelativeWhen mirrors batches.ts's toDisplayDate with the same unparseable-date-to-empty-string convention.

Cross-module data needs are satisfied by pass-by-parameter or by importing the other module's public domain/: tenancy's getProfileSnapshot takes the caller's Clerk user id because resolving it is modules/auth/data's private job; batches/data/metrics.ts and billing/data/billing.ts import docRecordFor/isDocTracked/isDocOnFile from modules/documents/domain/compliance. Since the mock-data retirement a data/ layer's only shared/ imports are types and pure helpers — billing.ts imports Batch/Tenant/DocumentRequirement from shared/types and nothing else from shared/.

domain/ layers are pure business rules with no I/O (urgencyTier, deriveDashboardMetrics, withTenantAccess) and are unit-tested with fixed as-of dates. shared/ may not re-export module code: the logic that once lived behind the shared/mocks facade (urgency, billing readiness, dashboard metrics) sits in module domain/ layers now, and dashboard metrics moved to modules/batches/domain/metrics.ts specifically because it had to import modules/documents/domain/compliance.

The per-module split of shared/types.ts is no longer blocked: RULES §2.16 strikes the old prohibition and CLAUDE.md records the split as unblocked, because the blocker was shared/mocks/seed.ts constructing 11 domain types in a layer that cannot import modules/ — and that dataset is gone. shared/README.md still documents the split as deferred, which is documentation drift; Batch's hub role remains a real design cost of splitting, not a boundary violation.

lib/supabase/ is the external data boundary: server.ts builds an anon-key client and attaches the caller's Clerk session token via the accessToken callback, throwing NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE (exported so callers can tell 'not signed in' from 'token rejected') instead of silently querying as anon, which RLS would answer with zero rows and no error; service.ts holds the RLS-bypassing service-role client reserved for server-to-server webhook provisioning, and ordinary write paths (tenancy/users.ts, import-export/learnerImport.ts) deliberately stay on the anon client so RLS decides.
No index barrels exist anywhere — deep imports are the convention (shared/README, CLAUDE.md); modules with no code yet hold a README naming their FR and planned contents.

The domains array in eslint.config.mjs (14 entries matching the modules/ directory exactly) is the single source that generates the per-module data/-privacy zones — adding a new module requires adding it there or that module's data/ is not made private to other modules.

Mappers are unit-tested in tests/unit/ against the real generated contract: batches.test.ts derives the module-private join-row fixture shape via Parameters<typeof mapBatchRow>[0] instead of duplicating it, and the tests/ directory sits outside the lint zones so test files may import database.types directly, even though app code may not; real-Supabase RLS/tenant-isolation integration tests are still outstanding.

After any migration, database.types.ts must be regenerated and then affected mappers and domain types updated; migrations are additive and supabase/migrations/20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql is the canonical schema + RLS migration.

The 'no row means missing' document backfill is a data-layer decision (batches.ts and documents.ts seed every catalog requirement with MISSING_DOC, then overlay submitted rows), and a key still absent after backfill means untracked — to be read via modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts, never by indexing the map directly.

Derive-layer sentinels protect downstream math: daysUntil returns Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY for a missing or unparseable date (the 'no known deadline' sentinel that sorts last and never trips urgencyTier, since NaN would silently corrupt sorting), toDisplayDate and activity.ts's toRelativeWhen return '' rather than 'Invalid Date', and the sentinel is kept out of printable copy by DashboardKpiGrid's Number.isFinite check ('no deadline set').

lib/supabase/database.types.ts is currently hand-maintained rather than regenerated: its header records that the ADR-006 tables/columns/RPCs were written by hand from migration 20260906130000 and verified against a generator run, and every table's Relationships is stubbed as [], which is what forces the as-casts on embedded-join rows in batches.ts, activity.ts, tenancy.ts and users.ts.

getBatchesSnapshot, getProfileSnapshot and getPlatformAdminSnapshot are wrapped in React cache() because app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx and each page in the route group call them independently within one request (the layout reads the profile for the admin nav row and the batch snapshot for MetricsRow); cache() scopes the sharing to that request, so a later navigation re-queries.

no-tenant-access is never produced by a query — RLS reports an unattached caller as a successful empty read — so the route folds it in with withTenantAccess(snapshot, access), which replaces only an ok snapshot so a real sync-failed/unconfigured is never masked, and treats access 'unknown' as no rewrite ('we could not check' must not render as 'you have no school'). Eight dashboard routes branch on the folded state to shared/ui/NoTenantAccessState instead of their ordinary empty state.

Screen guards follow a fixed order — denied, then sync-failed-with-zero-rows, then no-tenant-access, then empty, then no-results — because both sync-failed and no-tenant-access yield zero rows: checking empty first would swallow the retry banner behind a 'no batches, import one' message, and checking empty before no-tenant-access would offer an action the caller cannot perform. The no-results state comes last and lives in the client island, since it is a fact about filters rather than the snapshot.

Some files live in app/ rather than in a module precisely because they compose two modules' private data/ layers: app/(dashboard)/tenant-access.ts joins auth's getAuthUserId with tenancy's getProfileSnapshot (using the local token read rather than getCurrentUser's Clerk API fetch, since only the id is needed), and the (dashboard)/*/new/actions.ts Server Actions join tenancy's Postgres write with auth's Clerk invitation. Each encodes no business rule — validation and writes are delegated to domain/ and data/.

The four states are applied selectively, not uniformly: DocumentRequirementsSnapshot deliberately has no no-tenant-access member because the requirement catalog is per-program reference data (an empty catalog means unseeded, not unauthorized), and PlatformAdminSnapshot omits it because the verdict comes from a security-definer RPC about the caller rather than a tenant-scoped table.

Mock-data retirement is a contract change, not just a file deletion: batches.ts and activity.ts record that the MOCK_BATCHES / MOCK_ACTIVITY datasets they used to fall back to were deleted, no read path substitutes fabricated rows, and the remaining mentions are stale comments — shared/README.md still calls mocks/ the unconfigured fallback and isSupabaseConfigured's docblock still says 'silent mock fallback'.

Dashboard metric derivation has two homes, only one of which is live: modules/batches/domain/metrics.ts's deriveDashboardMetrics is called by the dashboard route and the shell layout, while modules/batches/data/metrics.ts's getDashboardMetrics (TES-30, derive-only, criticalDocumentKeys parameter) has no callers in app/, modules/ or tests/. Both guarantee every number is computed from the inputs rather than hardcoded.

The document-requirement catalog is always passed in as a parameter and callers pass [] today, because the live catalog (program_document_requirements) is scoped per scholarship program while Batch carries no resolvable program id — and the empty catalog is designed to degrade to 'unknown' (docCompliancePct null) and 'not ready' (billingGate's requiredTotal > 0), never to a fabricated pass.

Write paths return a discriminated state instead of throwing: a thrown Server Action error reaches the browser as an opaque digest that hides whether anything was written, so createUserAction returns denied/failed/unconfigured and importLearnersCsv returns validation-failed/sync-failed/ok — with unconfigured meaning the caller must disable the importer rather than pretend the import ran.

The supabase/migrations/ ledger is the seven additive migrations on top of the canonical 20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql (schema + RLS, which also idempotently seeds tenants, TWSP/CFSP programs, and the 8-key requirement catalog): 20260705070510 adds the trainer_credentials table with RLS; 20260717054607 is a guarded corrective that copies the lone AKB record out of the hand-made, non-conforming public.tenant (singular) table into the canonical tenants table and drops the rogue table, short-circuiting on databases rebuilt from the history where the table never existed; 20260831120000 seeds DEV-prefixed fixture batches/learners/documents ported from the then-present shared/mocks/seed.ts with NULL official_system_reference and adds the unique documents (batch_id, document_key) index; 20260904120000 adds the user-admin write policies; 20260906120000 adds the ensure_profile_tenant_membership function that applies an invitation's membership atomically; 20260906130000 adds the ADR-006 school registry and platform-admin RLS + RPCs.
